validity.researcher_notes: Diameter, capacity and status match the sheet. The Kursk encyclopedia gives operation from late 1959, matching the sheet, while the Kursk region page gives 1960. The 1020 mm figure is the later parallel line according to Ukrainian Wikipedia, where the first lines were 700 and 800 mm.

fills.researcher_notes: The Kursk region government page, read through the December 2022 archived copy, describes the Shebelinka, Kursk and Bryansk pipeline in the region. It gives a capacity of 13 million cubic meters a day, a diameter of 1020 mm and a working pressure of 55 atmospheres. The sheet value is the same. The figures sit in the region's description of the pipeline, so the tier is medium.

The Kursk region government page, read through the December 2022 archived copy, gives a pipe diameter of 1020 mm for the Shebelinka, Kursk and Bryansk pipeline. The sheet value is the same. The page describes the Kursk region stretch of 165.7 km, so the tier is medium. The Ukrainian Wikipedia page already on the sheet says the first lines were 700 and 800 mm and that 1020 mm is a later parallel line.

The Kursk Encyclopedia entry says laying finished in July 1959 and that gas began to flow to industry and homes in November and December 1959. The sheet start year of 1959 is the same. The Kursk region government page gives 1960 as the start of operation, so one source differs by a year.

Interfax reported on 27 October 2022 that Gazprom finished rebuilding a 40 km stretch of this pipeline near Belgorod and that Rostekhnadzor, the federal technical regulator, accepted the work. That shows the pipeline in use in late 2022. The sheet status of operating is the same. No newer citation was harvested.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Interfax reported in October 2022 that the pipeline was rebuilt near Belgorod and accepted by the regulator. No newer citation was harvested. The route also crosses a front-line area, so a later check for damage is worthwhile.

cross_row_leads.note: A later search could check for damage or outages to the Shebelinka to Belgorod, Kursk and Bryansk pipeline since 2022, since the Belgorod and Kursk regions have been shelled.
